newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine expects Yeltsin May 30 - foreign ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine expects Yeltsin May 30 - foreign ministry.

text.p: Ukraine is expecting on May 30 and 31 a much-postponed visit by Russian President Boris Yeltsin to sign a post-Soviet political deal, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

"There is no official programme yet, but the Ukrainian side is already preparing for these dates and so far there is no information of any postponement," said Olexander Ovcharov, deputy head of the ministry's information department.
Yeltsin has cancelled at least six trips to sign a political treaty with Ukraine over disagreements about the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet based on the Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea.

The presidential administration said in a press release that President Leonid Kuchma met Russian Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov on Monday to discuss bilateral relations and the programme of the visit which was "planned for the end of May".
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is expected to visit Ukraine on May 28 to 29 to pave the way for his president's visit.
Russia has the lion's share of the Black Sea Fleet but the two countries have so far been unable to agree exactly where and on what terms the ships should be based.

Interfax news agency said the Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Kiev on Monday had formed three commissions -- on the Fleet, on trade and economic cooperation and on settling the issue of former Soviet debts.
